wording_en: I can recognise common functions for which GenAI systems are used.
I understand that GenAI output is generated probabilistically and can be inaccurate.
I can identify situations in which GenAI is and is not an appropriate tool.
I can formulate prompts that communicate the task and constraints clearly.
I can refine my instructions when an initial GenAI response is inadequate.
I can integrate useful GenAI output into my own learning/teaching work.
I can assess whether a GenAI response is factually and logically sound.
I verify important GenAI claims using independent evidence.
I can detect omissions, bias, or unjustified confidence in GenAI output.
I consider privacy and data-protection risks before using GenAI.
I consider authorship, attribution, and academic/professional integrity.
I retain personal responsibility for decisions informed by GenAI.
Frequency of using GenAI to obtain explanations or clarify concepts.
Frequency of using GenAI to generate ideas or initial plans.
Frequency of using GenAI to review, revise, or improve existing work.
Frequency of using GenAI to produce substantial drafts or task outputs.
Frequency of using GenAI to complete complex tasks that would otherwise require substantial independent work.
I expect GenAI to provide generally competent assistance for suitable tasks.
I believe GenAI recommendations are dependable when I can verify them.
I am willing to rely on GenAI when completing relevant tasks.
Using GenAI has become something I do automatically in relevant situations.
When a suitable task appears, using GenAI is one of my first reactions.
I use GenAI with little conscious deliberation in familiar task settings.
GenAI errors could lead me to make poor learning/teaching decisions.
Relying on GenAI may weaken my ability to evaluate work independently.
Using GenAI for consequential tasks may create academic/professional problems.

I take responsibility for the quality of my learning outcomes.

I can design learning activities that use digital tools purposefully.
I adapt instructional materials to different learner needs.
I evaluate whether an instructional innovation improves learning.
I can revise AI-supported teaching designs after evidence or feedback.
I can integrate GenAI without surrendering professional judgement.
I find it difficult to begin some learning tasks without GenAI assistance.
I feel less confident completing familiar academic tasks when GenAI is unavailable.
I rely on GenAI even when I could complete the task independently.
I repeatedly check GenAI before finalising my own answer.

I prefer GenAI guidance to making an unaided judgement.
I use GenAI longer or more often than I originally intend.

Using GenAI enables me to complete relevant tasks more efficiently.
GenAI is useful for accomplishing important learning/teaching tasks.
Learning to use GenAI for my tasks is easy for me.
My interaction with GenAI is clear and understandable.
It is easy for me to become skilful at using GenAI.
People who are important to me think that I should use GenAI for relevant tasks.
People whose opinions I value encourage me to use GenAI.
People in my study/work environment commonly expect GenAI to be used.
I have the technical resources needed to use GenAI.
I have the knowledge and support needed to use GenAI effectively.
GenAI is compatible with the digital systems available for my learning/teaching work.

The benefits of GenAI are accessible across learners/teachers with different backgrounds.
GenAI encourages me to continue learning beyond immediate task requirements.
I use GenAI to explore knowledge or skills beyond what is currently required.
